# ColorTree

## Summary

The `ColorTree` card renders the Munsell color solid as an interactive 3D specimen and saves a picked color (`selectedColor`) with its Munsell notation (`selectedMunsell`). It is an exploratory study of color perception, after John Maeda — built primarily as a learning device that shows how Munsell's measured, lopsided color solid differs from Itten's idealized sphere — with three display formats: isolated (the full app), embedded, and fitted.

## What an AI can reuse or learn from this card

- `utils/munsell` — pure, dependency-free perceptual color math: `maxChroma` (each hue's peak chroma at its own value — the lopsided-canopy rule), `chipHex`/`munsellNotation` (Munsell → sRGB hex / notation), `buildArrays` (dual baked positions, tree and sphere, for GPU morphing).
- `utils/tree-engine` — a three.js engine pattern: shared shader uniforms eased toward spring targets, analytic screen→page picking without a raycaster, and a scissor-rendered miniature in the same canvas.
- `utils/shaders` — a three-address GLSL vertex morph (tree ↔ sphere ↔ flat atlas page).
- `components/color-tree-isolated` — a WebAudio ambient-sound layer (noise room tone + sine pad, event voices for morph/scrub/copy) that any card can adapt.

Discovery terms: color picker, Munsell, Itten, color theory, 3D color space, hue value chroma, perceptual color.

## Import

```javascript
import { ColorTree } from '../color-tree';
```

## Usage as a Field

You can use the `ColorTree` card as a field within a consuming card or field. Here's an example:

```gts
export class MyCard extends CardDef {
  @field colorTree = contains(ColorTree);
}
```

## Template Usage

To use the `ColorTree` card inside a template, you can do the following:

```hbs
<@fields.colorTree @format="isolated" />
```

This will render the `ColorTree` card in its isolated format.

For the embedded and fitted formats, you can use:

```hbs
<@fields.colorTree @format="embedded" />
<@fields.colorTree @format="fitted" />
```
